questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute work done by a constant force
questions.stem: A 4.0 kg crate is pushed 3.0 m across a floor by a 12 N horizontal force. How much work is done by the applied force in joules?
questions.explanation: Work equals force times displacement when they are parallel, giving 12 times 3.0 equals 36 J. The mass is irrelevant here. A common slip is to multiply mass by distance instead.
questions.hint: Use W = F d cos theta with theta zero.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify direction of static friction
questions.stem: A person pushes a heavy crate to the right, but it does not move. Which way does static friction on the crate act?

options.text: To the right, aiding the push.
Downward, adding to weight.
Upward, balancing weight.
To the left, opposing the push.

questions.explanation: Static friction opposes the tendency to move, so it points left against the push. It does not aid motion.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Relate kinetic energy to speed squared
questions.stem: If a car's speed doubles, how does its kinetic energy change?

options.text: It quadruples.
It stays the same.
It doubles.
It halves.

questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is 0.5 m v squared, so doubling speed quadruples KE. This is why stopping distance grows sharply.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why normal force can exceed weight
questions.stem: Why can the normal force on an object exceed its weight?

options.text: Because normal force is always equal to weight.
Because weight decreases when normal increases.
Because normal force is a vector sum of weight.
Because acceleration or other forces add vertical components.

questions.explanation: Normal force adjusts to prevent penetration; vertical acceleration or angled forces can make it larger than mg. It is not locked to weight.
questions.hint: N balances all vertical forces and acceleration.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute work for cubic force
questions.stem: A force F = 4 x^3 N acts from x = 0 to x = 1.0 m. What work is done in joules?
questions.explanation: Integrate 4 x^3 dx = x^4 from 0 to 1 = 1 J. Using 4 times 1 cubed gives 4, missing integration.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compare drag on objects of different shape
questions.stem: At the same speed, which shape experiences greater air drag: a flat plate or a streamlined body of equal area?

options.text: The flat plate, because it disrupts flow more.
The streamlined body, because smooth flow increases drag.
Both equal, because area is equal.
Neither, because drag is zero at constant speed.

questions.explanation: Drag depends on drag coefficient; a flat plate has higher C_d than a streamlined body, so more drag at equal area and speed.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Relate period and frequency
questions.stem: What is the relationship between period T and frequency f of circular motion?

options.text: T = f.
T = 2π f.

questions.explanation: Period is the reciprocal of frequency: T = 1/f. Angular frequency omega = 2π f, not period.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify forces on a block on a horizontal surface
questions.stem: A block slides on a horizontal floor with friction. Which forces act on it?

options.text: Kinetic friction only.
Weight and normal only.
Weight, normal, and an applied force.
Weight, normal, and kinetic friction.

questions.explanation: A sliding block on a horizontal surface has weight, normal, and kinetic friction. No applied force is mentioned, so none is included.
questions.hint: Include weight, normal, and kinetic friction.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain weight variation with altitude
questions.stem: Why does an object weigh slightly less at high altitude than at sea level?

options.text: Because mass decreases with altitude.
Because air resistance reduces weight.
options.misconception: invokes drag on a stationary object

options.text: Because gravitational field weakens with distance from Earth's center.
Because normal force increases with altitude.

questions.explanation: Weight depends on g, which decreases with distance from Earth's center. Mass is unchanged.
questions.hint: g varies with distance from center.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute max static friction force
questions.stem: A 20 kg crate on a floor has mu_s = 0.60. What is the maximum static friction in newtons? Use g = 9.8.
questions.explanation: f_max = mu_s m g = 0.6*20*9.8 = 117.6 N. Using mu_k would underestimate for static case.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute work by gravity on a ramp
questions.stem: A 5.0 kg block descends 3.0 m vertically along a ramp. How much work does gravity do in joules? Use g = 9.8.
questions.explanation: Work by gravity depends only on vertical displacement: mg h = 5*9.8*3 = 147 J. Path length is irrelevant.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute normal on an incline with acceleration
questions.stem: A block on a frictionless incline accelerates down the plane. What is the normal force compared to mg cos theta?

options.text: Zero, because the block is accelerating.
Greater than mg cos theta, because motion increases normal.
Less than mg cos theta, because acceleration reduces normal.
Equal to mg cos theta, since acceleration is along the plane.

questions.explanation: Acceleration is along the plane, so perpendicular forces still balance: N = mg cos theta. No perpendicular acceleration exists.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute work from integral of sine force
questions.stem: A force F = 5 sin(x) N acts from x = 0 to x = pi/2. What work is done in joules?
questions.explanation: Integrate 5 sin x dx from 0 to pi/2: 5[-cos x]_0^{pi/2} = 5(0 - (-1)) = 5 J. Using 5 sin(pi/2)*pi/2 overcounts.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a parachute slows descent
questions.stem: Why does opening a parachute reduce a skydiver's terminal speed?

options.text: It increases the skydiver's mass.
It decreases gravity acting on the diver.
It increases drag area, so balance with weight occurs at lower speed.
It converts kinetic energy to potential energy.

questions.explanation: Larger area increases drag at a given speed, so equilibrium with weight occurs at a lower speed. Mass and gravity are unchanged.
